planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions or container stock in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained woodland soil in partial to full shade; established clumps require little care beyond an annual leaf-mold mulch.

directions: Rough-fruited fairybells is a Rocky Mountain and northern-forest native distinguished from other North American fairybells by the finely warty, rough-textured surface of its orange-red berries, which ripen in mid to late summer beneath arching, sparingly branched stems. The nodding, greenish-white to pale yellow bell flowers open in May and June at the tips of the foliage, easily overlooked among the paired, prominently veined leaves until the berries draw attention in fall. Give it cool, humus-rich soil with reliable moisture in dappled to deep shade beneath conifers or mixed woodland, where it slowly forms loose, spreading colonies alongside trilliums and native ferns. It resents summer drought and heavy clay, performing best where its wide native range already tells you it is happy: cool montane and boreal forest understories from British Columbia to the Southwest.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this miniature fairy bells stays low and slowly knits together into a fine-textured woodland carpet.

directions: Japanese fairy bells is a diminutive, rhizomatous woodland groundcover from Japan, Korea, and China, forming low tufts of olive-green, lance-shaped leaves only a few inches tall - far smaller in scale than its taller cousins Disporum sessile and D. cantoniense. Small, star-shaped, creamy-white flowers dangle just above the foliage in mid to late spring, followed by blue-black berries in fall. Site it in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in part to full shade as an intimate edging or underplanting for larger ferns and hostas, where its slow spread by rhizome is an asset rather than a liability. It is essentially trouble-free apart from the usual slug and snail watch, and rewards close inspection in a shaded rock garden or trough setting.

common_name: Dwarf Variegated Fairy Bells (Gold-Edged Chigo Yuri)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, fertile, acidic, well-drained soil in light to medium shade; this variegated selection spreads more slowly than the plain green species, so be patient while it fills in.

directions: This selection of the miniature Japanese fairy bells pairs the species' diminutive scale with each medium-green leaf neatly edged in gold, giving the low foliage mounds a bright, glowing quality in the shaded woodland garden even before the small, creamy-white, star-shaped flowers appear just above the leaves in mid-spring. It forms a dense, slow-spreading groundcover over several seasons, best used as a choice specimen or fine-textured edging near a path where its variegated foliage can be appreciated up close rather than lost among coarser neighbors. Grow in moist, fertile, acidic, well-drained soil in light to medium shade, mulching with leaf mold to keep roots cool; it combines well with mosses, dwarf ferns, and other small-scale woodland treasures. Divide congested clumps in early spring only when necessary, as it resents frequent disturbance.
